content: 1. Doravirine/lamivudine/tenofovir DF is a combination tablet containing 100 mg of doravirine, 300 mg of lamivudine, and 300 mg of tenofovir DF. It is administered orally once daily, with or without food. 2. Amobarbital reduces the plasma levels and efficacy of doravirine by inducing hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 enzymes. Co-administration is contraindicated due to the risk of reduced virologic response and potential resistance to doravirine. 3. Apalutamide decreases doravirine levels and effects through CYP3A4 enzyme induction. Co-administration is contraindicated, as it may lead to virologic failure and resistance. 4. Streptozocin and tenofovir DF both increase nephrotoxicity and/or ototoxicity. Co-administration is contraindicated. Streptozocin should not be used with other nephrotoxic agents. 35. Adefovir and tenofovir DF increase each other’s toxicity through pharmacodynamic synergy, leading to enhanced nephrotoxicity. Co-administration should be avoided or alternative drugs used. 37. Antiretroviral medications, including doravirine, lamivudine, and tenofovir DF, may interfere with the manufacturing of atidarsagene autotemcel. Avoid ARTs for at least one month before cell mobilization or until the medications are fully eliminated. 38. Bacitracin and tenofovir DF both increase nephrotoxicity and/or ototoxicity. Avoid concurrent use of bacitracin with other nephrotoxic drugs. 39. Cyclosporine and tenofovir DF both increase nephrotoxicity and/or ototoxicity. Co-administration should be avoided or alternative drugs used. 40. Tenofovir DF decreases the levels and effects of dabigatran and edoxaban by inducing P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporters. Co-administration should be avoided.
